title: Use script type for SharedWorkerGlobalScope matching
body:
In the specification for [Shared Worker interface](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#sharedworker), we use constructor origin, url and name for finding matching SharedWorkerGlobalScope.

> 10.2.6.4.11.2
If there exists a SharedWorkerGlobalScope object whose closing flag is false, constructor origin is same origin with outside settings's origin, constructor url equals urlRecord, and name equals the value of options's name member, then set worker global scope to that SharedWorkerGlobalScope object.

Here, I think we should use script type ('classic' or 'module') for matching process as well to make the model clearer. We don't expect to load the same scripts to the same worker with different script types.
For example, the current spec allow the following to run:

```
// import.js
import * as module from 'something.js'

// main.js
const module_worker = new SharedWorker('import.js', {type: 'module'});
const classic_worker = new SharedWorker('import.js', {type: 'classic'});
```
`classic_worker` seems to return SyntaxError since 'import.js' uses static import, but this script is already loaded when `module_worker` is constructed and it is not actually loaded in the second line of 'main.js', so SyntaxError doesn't occur if we use the same shared worker. This seems strange.

However, it is true that loading same codes with both 'classic' worker ad 'module' worker doesn't occur much, so it might be not a trouble in the practical meaning. (If the codes to load doesn't use static import, then loading via 'classic' type or 'module' type is a same thing in terms of behavior. If the codes includes static import, then loading via 'classic' type returns SyntaxError so loading via both 'classic' and 'module' cannot be a problem in the first place.)


Is this an issue for spec to modify?

/cc @domenic  @nhiroki
